headline: New law requires federal agencies to report each year on projects that are more than five years late or $1 billion over budget.
what_it_does: The White House budget office (OMB) must tell federal agencies to send it yearly information on federally funded projects that are more than five years behind schedule or have cost at least $1 billion more than first estimated. Agencies must describe each project, any changes to its scope, original and current completion dates, original and current cost estimates adjusted for inflation, reasons for delays or cost increases, and any bonuses or incentive fees paid. OMB must then send an annual report to Congress and post it on its website.

who_it_affects.how: They must collect and send yearly details to OMB about their projects that are far behind schedule or far over budget.
It must issue guidance to agencies, gather their information, and send a yearly public report to Congress.
Any bonuses, awards, or incentive fees they receive on delayed or over-budget projects will be listed, along with the reasons for them, in a public report.

who_it_affects.group: Members of Congress and the public
who_it_affects.how: They will get a yearly report, posted online, showing which federal projects are badly delayed or over budget and why.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 7, 2026; the summary does not give specific deadlines for the guidance or first report.
